subject: AWS Marketplace metering + fulfillment — integration matrix and next steps
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Kevin Sato <kevin.sato@amazon.com>, lena.ortiz@acme-corp.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: AWS Marketplace metering + fulfillment — integration matrix and next steps

Hi Kevin / Lena —

Following up from last week's call: Acme is ready to move forward with a Marketplace listing and needs clarity on metering, entitlement mapping, and the fulfillment contract. I've attached a draft integration matrix that maps our SaaS SKU/entitlements to AWS fulfillment flows (redwood_aws_integration_matrix.xlsx).

High level asks from Acme:
- Confirm entitlement model (seat-based vs. usage meter) for their customer tiering
- Confirm who signs the SaaS fulfillment contract and the timeline for approval
- Explain how billing reconciliation will work (AWS -> Acme -> Redwood) and what telemetry we need to expose

Kevin — can you share the standard AWS metering checklist and any timing constraints for a co-sell listing?
Lena — once we align on entitlement mapping, we'll put together a short mutual action plan (2–3 week canary + full launch cadence).

Attaching: redwood_aws_integration_matrix.xlsx, SaaS_fulfillment_contract_draft.docx

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Partnerships Program Manager
Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood_aws_integration_matrix.xlsx]
[attachment: SaaS_fulfillment_contract_draft.docx]

From: Kevin Sato <kevin.sato@amazon.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, lena.ortiz@acme-corp.com
Cc: Elena Kovacs <elena.kovacs@cloudbridge.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2026 11:24:00 -0800
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace metering + fulfillment — integration matrix and next steps

Hannah / Lena —

Thanks for the matrix, Hannah. I've attached the AWS metering checklist and the standard SaaS fulfillment terms we use for Marketplace listings (aws_metering_checklist.pdf). A few quick notes after a skim:

- Metering type: the seat + incremental usage hybrid works well for this profile (base monthly seat + API token-based metering for overage). That maps cleanly to Marketplace metering APIs.
- Entitlement flow: AWS issues an entitlement record on purchase; your system must reconcile customer identifiers and map to Redwood SKU IDs within 24 hours to avoid provisioning delays.
- Billing reconciliation: AWS will send usage records; the seller (Redwood) reports revenue and passes agreed settlement to Acme per your partner contract. If Acme wants to be billed directly via pass-through, we need a Marketplace seller-to-seller arrangement — can discuss with procurement.

I copied Elena from CloudBridge — they run the connector we typically recommend for entitlement sync and have a standard webhook pattern. Short timeline: once we have the contract signed, technical enablement typically takes 7–10 business days for a basic integration + extra if you need custom reconciliation logic.

Attached: aws_metering_checklist.pdf

—Kevin
Kevin Sato
AWS Marketplace Sales
[attachment: aws_metering_checklist.pdf]

From: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acme-corp.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Kevin Sato <kevin.sato@amazon.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2026 14:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace metering + fulfillment — integration matrix and next steps

Thanks Hannah / Kevin —

A couple of procurement questions before we proceed:
1) We need visibility into the billing reconciliation cadence and sample reports. Will Redwood provide a monthly invoice and a usage report that we can reconcile against AWS usage records?
2) For the entitlement IDs, what identifier should our systems expose so matches don't break (email vs. account-id vs. customer_ref)?
3) If we require pass-through billing (Acme billed directly by AWS), what additional contract steps are required?

We're aiming for a pilot with a subset of 50 enterprise seats for Q1 if timelines match.

-Lena
Lena Ortiz
Sr. Manager, Sourcing & Procurement
Acme Corp

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acme-corp.com>, Kevin Sato <kevin.sato@amazon.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Dec 2026 09:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace metering + fulfillment — integration matrix and next steps

Lena —

Good questions. Short answers up front, details below and I've attached the contract draft for legal review.

1) Reconciliation & reports: Redwood will produce a monthly usage export and invoice. We will align the CSV fields with the AWS usage report (usage_start, usage_end, customer_external_id, sku_id, quantity, price). We'll send a sample reconciliation CSV during the pilot week.

2) Entitlement identifier: recommend using Acme's "customer_external_id" (an immutable org-id) as the primary key; fall back to email only for user-scoped entitlements. We'll include a normalization step in the runbook to prevent duplicates.

3) Pass-through billing: this is possible but requires a seller-to-seller agreement on AWS (adds ~2 weeks to contracting) and a reconciliation SLA. If Acme prefers speed, the simpler path is Redwood invoicing Acme (standard seller flow) and Redwood redistributing the partner revenue per our partner agreement.

Action items (proposed):
- Kevin: confirm CloudBridge webhook sample and any required headers (due Thu 12/17)
- Elena/CloudBridge: provide connector endpoint spec (due Fri 12/18)
- Marissa/Redwood legal: quick turn on contract redlines (circa 5 business days)
- Ben/Redwood infra: checklist for telemetry fields (see note below)

Ben — note on telemetry: Include tokenized customer_external_id in the usage records, a transaction_id for reconciliation, and a minimal event payload to avoid PII transfer.

I'll schedule a short sync for Friday to confirm the mutual action plan.

Thanks,
Hannah
Senior Partnerships Program Manager
Redwood Inference
[attachment: SaaS_fulfillment_contract_draft.docx]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 15 Dec 2026 16:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace metering + fulfillment — integration matrix and next steps

Quick operational add:

- For reconciliation we should add a three-way check during pilot (AWS usage file vs Redwood reported usage vs Acme sample logs). Recommend automating a nightly digest and an endpoint for ad-hoc pulls.
- We'll include a reconciliation_status column on the monthly CSV and a transaction-level checksum to speed investigations.
- Canary window suggestion: Jan 10–17 for the 50-seat pilot, with rollback on any reconciliation mismatch > 0.5% for two consecutive days.

Jonas — can you confirm availability for a short post-launch incident playbook review?

-ben
Ben Carter
Director, Platform Partnerships
Redwood Inference
